release_summary.summary: The problem, as formally defined in PD-1, is that dispute tickets roughly doubled at the August 2026 boundary (E-06) and that 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are on ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads (E-02) -- ruling out field-read shortfalls and AMI/MDMS delivery failure as the majority cause and pointing instead to a likely billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), best supported by E-10's finding that most ESTIMATED-read disputes involve valid, on-time AMI reads rejected for \"high consumption\" by billing import. This differs from the original stakeholder request (CL-01: build an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills), which was treated as an unverified hypothesis and partly disproven -- several alternative causes (slow response times, tariff errors, field staffing, AMI delivery failure) were explicitly tested and rejected with evidence. The DEFINE Gate returned only a CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical/high unknowns (root-cause rule-change confirmation and a legitimate-usage-spike alternative) as open verification obligations. Given that, the release itself is narrow: only two safe, non-mutating work items went out -- updating CRM dispute response templates and monitoring MDMS export access status -- with no bill correction, account flagging, or automated bill writes, consistent with the no-auto-bill-write constraint. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the two still-open verification obligations block only scope outside what was actually released, so the limited release could proceed while deeper remediation (confirming the rule change, correcting it, flagging/fixing affected accounts) remains blocked pending that confirmation and vendor access.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): dispute tickets abruptly roughly doubled at the August 2026 boundary (E-06), and 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were on ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), so estimate-substitution mechanisms (field-read shortfalls, AMI/MDMS delivery failure) cannot be the majority cause.

The original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills; this framing was tested as a hypothesis, not accepted as fact, per the harness's evidence discipline.

Competing causes were tested and rejected with evidence: slow ticket response (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING) rejected by E-01, E-04 (response times are within SLA); tariff/rate error (H-TARIFF-RATE-ERROR) rejected by E-03, E-05 (no logged tariff change); field-read failure (H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE) rejected by E-02 (doesn't explain ACTUAL-read majority); AMI/MDMS delivery failure (H-AMI-MDMS-READ-FAILURE) rejected by E-02, E-10.

The best-supported remaining mechanism is a billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, CANDIDATE), supported by E-02 and E-10, which shows 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes involve valid AMI reads received on time but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION by billing import (E-10) -- pointing at a rule, not a delivery failure.

This root cause is not yet confirmed: two verification obligations (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED, VOB-U-USAGE-SPIKE-ALT) remain OPEN, and the DEFINE Gate result was only CONDITIONAL_PASS with these deferred as VOBs.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): dispute tickets abruptly roughly doubled at the August 2026 boundary (E-06), and 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were on ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), so estimate-substitution mechanisms (field-read shortfalls, AMI/MDMS delivery failure) cannot be the majority cause.

The original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills; this framing was tested as a hypothesis, not accepted as fact, per the harness's evidence discipline.

Competing causes were tested and rejected with evidence: slow ticket response (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING) rejected by E-01, E-04 (response times are within SLA); tariff/rate error (H-TARIFF-RATE-ERROR) rejected by E-03, E-05 (no logged tariff change); field-read failure (H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE) rejected by E-02 (doesn't explain ACTUAL-read majority); AMI/MDMS delivery failure (H-AMI-MDMS-READ-FAILURE) rejected by E-02, E-10.

The best-supported remaining mechanism is a billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, CANDIDATE), supported by E-02 and E-10, which shows 1184 of 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes involve valid AMI reads received on time but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION by billing import (E-10) -- pointing at a rule, not a delivery failure.

This root cause is not yet confirmed: two verification obligations (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED, VOB-U-USAGE-SPIKE-ALT) remain OPEN, and the DEFINE Gate result was only CONDITIONAL_PASS with these deferred as VOBs.

What was released (release_scope in SD-1): only two low-risk, non-mutating work items -- updating CRM dispute ticket response templates (W-WI-UPDATE-TEMPLATES, DA-TICKET) and monitoring MDMS export access status (W-WI-MONITOR-MDMS, DA-MDMS). No bill correction, no account flagging, and no automated bill writes are included, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint and success criterion SC-NO-AUTO-BILL-WRITE.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with an empty hold list: the two open VOBs' blocking_scope (query_billing_rule_change_log, flag_accounts_for_manual_bill_review, segment_dispute_tickets_by_cause) lies outside the actual release scope, so the narrow template/monitoring release could proceed while deeper remediation stays blocked.

No bill correction occurs in this release, so the core metrics (M-DISPUTE-VOLUME at 1260 vs a 600 target; the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes) are not yet addressed; any billing correction candidate found by future analysis must go to Billing Operations for manual adjustment, since automated bill writes are out of scope by design (K-BILLWRITE).
limitations_explained: Two critical/high unknowns remain OPEN and unresolved: VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED (whether billing-config actually shows an August rule change) and VOB-U-USAGE-SPIKE-ALT (whether part of the ACTUAL-read disputes reflect legitimate seasonal usage rather than a defect) -- both deferred past this release.
Because the root cause is unconfirmed, the released ticket response templates cannot yet reference a specific confirmed cause; they are generic pending resolution of the two open VOBs.

AMI/MDMS read-delivery cannot be independently verified for the ESTIMATED-read dispute segment because vendor-provisioned mdms-export access was still pending as of the formal state, and the mdms-export tool itself is DEGRADED, so the monitoring work item can only report access status, not verify read-delivery correctness.

No billing correction or defect-account flagging happens in this release; the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes and the M-DISPUTE-VOLUME metric (currently 1260/month vs a 600 target) remain unaddressed by this release and require future, human-approved action.

Any eventual billing correction identified by further analysis must be handed to Billing Operations for manual adjustment -- automated bill writes are categorically out of scope per the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint, regardless of what root-cause confirmation later shows.

A stakeholder claim (SH-AMI, E-09/CL-04) that MDMS export access is now provisioned is non-authoritative and unverified; it has not been confirmed to resolve the underlying access or verification gap.
output.summary: The problem, as formally defined in PD-1, is that dispute tickets roughly doubled at the August 2026 boundary (E-06) and that 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are on ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads (E-02) -- ruling out field-read shortfalls and AMI/MDMS delivery failure as the majority cause and pointing instead to a likely billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), best supported by E-10's finding that most ESTIMATED-read disputes involve valid, on-time AMI reads rejected for \"high consumption\" by billing import. This differs from the original stakeholder request (CL-01: build an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills), which was treated as an unverified hypothesis and partly disproven -- several alternative causes (slow response times, tariff errors, field staffing, AMI delivery failure) were explicitly tested and rejected with evidence. The DEFINE Gate returned only a CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical/high unknowns (root-cause rule-change confirmation and a legitimate-usage-spike alternative) as open verification obligations. Given that, the release itself is narrow: only two safe, non-mutating work items went out -- updating CRM dispute response templates and monitoring MDMS export access status -- with no bill correction, account flagging, or automated bill writes, consistent with the no-auto-bill-write constraint. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the two still-open verification obligations block only scope outside what was actually released, so the limited release could proceed while deeper remediation (confirming the rule change, correcting it, flagging/fixing affected accounts) remains blocked pending that confirmation and vendor access.
